name: Kenji Kasahara
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Kenji Kasahara founded social networking site Mixi in 2004; it went public in 2006.
In 2013 Mixi was losing customers and investors as competitors raced ahead.
Kasahara stepped down as CEO but stayed on as chairman.
He refocused the business on mobile gaming, e-commerce, dating and apartment hunting.
Mixi's popular Monster Strike game has been downloaded tens of millions of times.

name: Gina Vecchiarelli
forbes_bio: Gina Vecchiarelli and her sister Terry Leprino inherited a 90% stake in $3.6 billion (estimated annual revenue) Leprino Foods after the death of their father James Leprino in June 2025.
James Leprino built the company his father founded in 1950 into the world's largest mozzarella cheese maker, after pioneering the technology for manufacturing pizza cheese at scale.
Leprino manufactures and sells more than 1 billion pounds of cheese annually and supplies cheese to Domino's, Pizza Hut, Papa John's and other pizza brands.
Vecchiarelli's husband Dan Vecchiarelli took over as chairman and CEO of Leprino Foods around 2023.

Gina Vecchiarelli has kept a low profile, but her father told Forbes in 2016 that she was "running a program for Make-A-Wish" and that she was focused on mothering her two daughters, who were about to graduate from college.

name: Jet Jie Li
forbes_bio: Jet Jie Li is the chairman and CEO of package delivery company J&T Global Express.
Li set up J&T in Jakarta in 2015 after leading Chinese smartphone maker OPPO's expansion in Indonesia and other Asian countries.
Today the company counts China as its largest market, followed by Southeast Asia where it is the market leader by parcel volume.
J&T went public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2023.

name: Wee Wei Chi
forbes_bio: Wee Wei Chi is the younger daughter of late patriarch Wee Cho Yaw, cofounder of United Overseas Bank, one of Singapore's largest banks.
She sits on the board of Kheng Leong, the family's commercial property development and investment outfit.
Her husband, David Eu, is from the family that founded Eu Yan Sang, a traditional Chinese medicine company in Singapore.
She has a bachelor's degree in fine arts from Moravian University in Pennsylvania.

name: Chen Huwen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026); Hurun China (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: Chen Huwen is the chairman and a co-founder of Shanghai M&G Stationary Inc.
M&G Stationary was founded in 1996.
Chen holds an EMBA degree and has been involved in stationery manufacturing since 1997.

name: Shashank Kumar
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Shashank Kumar cofounded financial services firm Razorpay, which operates India's largest payment gateway by number of transactions processed.
Privately held Razorpay was last valued at $7.5 billion after raising more than $700 million over multiple funding rounds.
Marquee investors include private equity players such as Singapore's sovereign wealth fund GIC and U.S. private equity giant TVC Capital.
Credit card giant Mastercard also holds a stake.
It caters to the startup space serving 113 of the top 125 unicorns in India.
forbes_facts: It has acquired eight businesses to date including a payroll management outfit and a point-of-sale platform.
He has a B. Tech degree from India's elite Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee.

name: Andrea Della Valle
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2018); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Andrea Della Valle and his brother, Diego, are billionaires thanks to their majority ownership of Italian luxury goods maker Tod's S.p.A.
He is the vice chairman of the global shoe- and purse-maker that his grandfather founded in the early 1900s as a small shoe factory.
In 2024, the brothers teamed up with private equity firm L Catterton and LVMH to take Tod's private at a $1.5 billion valuation.
The brothers also own stakes in Vespa-maker Piaggio and media conglomerate RCS MediaGroup.
Andrea was chairman of soccer team ACF Fiorentina until 2009, helping turn the club around after its previous owner drove it into bankruptcy.

name: JoeBen Bevirt
sec_insider_companies: Joby Aviation, Inc. (JOBY) - CEO and Chief Architect
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Hurun Global (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: JoeBen Bevirt is the founder and CEO of Joby Aviation, which is developing aircraft capable of taking off and landing vertically.

Raised on an off-the-grid commune in California, as a kid Bevirt dreamed of planes that could maneuver like helicopters, and went on to study engineering at the University of California at Davis and Stanford.
He launched Joby in 2009 after first founding Velocity11, which built liquid-handling robots used for testing potential drugs, and the company behind GorillaPod, a flexible camera tripod.
He raised funds from the likes of carmaker Toyota, Laurene Powell Jobs' Emerson Collective and Jeff Skoll's Capricorn Investment Group, and took Joby public via SPAC merger in 2021.
forbes_facts: Bevirt's father was a member of author Ken Kesey's Merry Pranksters group. He's named JoeBen after a character in Kesey's novel "Sometimes a Great Notion."

name: Yaohai Wang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022-2026); Forbes annual (2017-2021); Hurun Global (2015-2021); Hurun China (2008-2017)
forbes_bio: Wang Yaohai chairs Opple Lighting, one of China's largest lighting makers.
Wang cofounded Opple with his wife Ma Xiuhui, fellow billionaire, in 1996 in Zhongshan, a major lighting manufacturing center, with only six workers.
Today, Opple employs more than 5600 people and makes traditional lamps, electrical appliances and kitchen ceiling products.

name: Zhang Wen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Hurun China (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2025)
forbes_bio: Zhang Wen is the chairman and CEO of Shanghai Biren Technology, a fabless maker of high-performance GPU chips and provider of software for intelligent computing.
Zhang founded the company in 2019 and took it public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in January 2026.
Zhang worked as the president at China's AI software heavyweight SenseTime Group before striking out on his own.
forbes_facts: Zhang earned a Juris Doctor degree from Harvard University and practiced law in New York State before returning to China.
